title: Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM): what it does with findings, and what can be automated

prose.text: UVM manages vulnerability findings that other tools produce; ingestion is covered in [[uvm.anysource]]. {{what-it-is}}

prose.label: Workflows and reporting.
prose.text: {{workflows}} Saved reports and their export, including the Reporting API, are platform-wide: [[portfolio.secops-platform:report-schedule]], [[portfolio.secops-platform:reporting-api]].

{{no-client-surface}} Ingestion has an Upload File API whose contract is open ([[uvm.anysource]]), and export goes through the platform's Reporting API ([[portfolio.secops-platform:reporting-api-contract]]).

checks.do: For automating UVM, separate ingestion (AnySource, including the Upload File API) from export (saved reports and the Reporting API); no client covers either.

what-it-is.statement: UVM provides a single place for managing vulnerabilities, simplifying the process of identifying and remediating security risks.

quotes: Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM) provides a single place for managing vulnerabilities, simplifying the process of identifying and remediating security risks.

prioritization.statement: Zscaler's UVM product page describes risk prioritization with contextual insight into risk factors and mitigating controls, out-of-the-box multifactor scoring that accounts for risk factors and mitigating controls, and adjustable weights for any risk factor or mitigating control.

quotes: Identify your biggest risks with contextual insights into your risk factors and mitigating controls.
Out-of-the-Box Multifactor Scoring Understand your top risks with prebuilt risk calculation that accounts for your risk factors and mitigating controls.
Customizable Factors and Weights Adjust the weight of any risk factor or mitigating control based on your specific needs, unlike the static weights of traditional vulnerability management tools.

marketing-downgraded.statement: Zscaler's UVM product page says 80% of "critical" issues are downgraded to "medium".

correlation.statement: The product page says UVM is powered by the Data Fabric for Security, which ingests data from vulnerability and exploitability sources, Zscaler and third parties through 150+ prebuilt data connectors, and correlates security findings and context spanning identity, assets, user behavior, mitigating controls, business processes and organizational hierarchy.

quotes: UVM is powered by our Data Fabric for Security, which ingests data from traditional vulnerability and exploitability sources—as well as Zscaler and third parties—leveraging 150+ prebuilt data connectors.
It correlates security findings and context spanning identity, assets, user behavior, mitigating controls, business processes, organizational hierarchy, and more.

workflows.statement: The product page lists prebuilt dashboards and reports, custom dashboards and reports, custom workflows that match the organizational structure, two-way ticketing integration that reconciles tickets including automatic closing and reopening, and exception management for requesting and approving extensions when remediations cannot be completed within SLAs.

quotes: Prebuilt Dashboards and Reports Simplify reporting with an array of readymade reports that capture risk posture, remediation history, asset coverage, and more.
Custom Dashboards and Reports Easily create your own reports and dashboards to show SLA performance, KPI status, and more.
Custom Workflows Take effective action with workflows that match your organizational structure to get the right teams the right info at the right time.
Two-Way Ticketing Integration Automatically reconcile tickets, including automatic closing and reopening, to gain an accurate view of remediation requests.
Exception Management Request and approve extensions with context when remediations cannot be completed within SLAs, improving efficiency and transparency.

no-client-surface.statement: No vendored client covers UVM: the Go and Python SDKs, the Terraform providers, the Ansible collections, the MCP server, the OneAPI Postman collection and the captured Automate contract have no UVM service.

quotes: used in your server-side code to interact with the Zscaler API platform across multiple products such as:

no-client-surface.conditions: Rests on an absence. The Python README's product list (introduced by the quoted line) names no UVM API, and at the pins `git grep -i -E 'unified.vulnerability|\buvm\b'` finds no UVM code in the Go or Python SDKs, the ZIA, ZPA, ZCC or ZTC providers, the Ansible collections or the MCP server; the Postman collection has no match. The MCP server's EASM and ZMS tools are separate products.
